intent: Parse human-entered money amounts into exact integer cents for billing.
constraints: Keep the public signature parse_cents(amount: str) -> int.
Use only the Python standard library.
Support ordinary signed or unsigned decimal strings, allowing surrounding whitespace.
Stage 1 deliberately left accounting-style parentheses unsupported; the outstanding next step (stage 2) now adds them.
Work only on this small evaluation project; do not inspect eval runners, other runs or sibling fixtures.
Edit only money.py and ignored [PRIVATE REFERENCE] files; Remvu init may update .gitignore.
Use the actual local Remvu runtime without installing it globally.
Do not commit, generate the public file, install hooks or complete the outstanding step.
rejected_directions: Do not use binary floating-point arithmetic for monetary conversion.
next_step: Accept accounting-style parenthesized negative amounts such as (12.345) as -1235 cents, while keeping ordinary signed amounts and Decimal ROUND_HALF_UP behavior. Edit money.py only.
known_failed_checks: MONEY_ACCOUNTING: python3 -c 'from money import parse_cents; assert parse_cents("(12.345)") == -1235' failed with decimal.InvalidOperation (ConversionSyntax), exit code 1, before the accounting-parentheses change.
